title: Banosh (Hutsul cornmeal porridge with sour cream, mushrooms and cheese)

ingredients.name: feta or other crumbly brined sheep's cheese (bryndza substitute)
crispy bacon or pork crackling to serve (optional)

steps: Bring the sour cream and water to a gentle simmer with the salt in a heavy pot.
Slowly pour in the cornmeal, whisking so no lumps form, then lower the heat.
Cook for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring often with a wooden spoon, until thick and the cornmeal is soft; add a splash more cream or water if it gets too stiff.
Meanwhile fry the onion and mushrooms in the butter until golden and any liquid has gone.
Spoon the banosh into warm bowls, top with the mushrooms and crumbled cheese, and add crisp bacon if you wish.
Serve immediately while it is hot and creamy.

title: Chicken Kyiv (breaded chicken fillet rolled around garlic butter)

ingredients.name: skinless chicken breast fillets (about 180 g each)

steps: Mash the butter with the garlic, herbs and a pinch of salt, shape it into a log, wrap it and freeze it for 30 minutes until hard.
Cut a pocket lengthwise into each chicken breast, or butterfly it, and pound the meat gently between sheets of baking paper to an even thickness without tearing it.
Season the chicken, cut the cold butter into 4 pieces and place one in the centre of each fillet.
Fold the sides over the butter and roll up tightly into a neat parcel, tucking in the edges so that the butter cannot leak.
Coat each parcel in flour, then beaten egg, then breadcrumbs; dip it in egg and crumbs a second time for a thicker crust and chill for 20 minutes.
Heat the oil to about 170 C (340 F) in a deep pan and fry the parcels for 5 to 6 minutes, turning, until deep golden.
Transfer them to a tray and bake at 180 C (350 F) for 10 to 15 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and the juices run clear.
Rest for 2 minutes and serve with mashed potatoes or buttered vegetables; the garlic butter will run out when it is cut.

title: Hrechanyky (Ukrainian buckwheat and meat patties)

ingredients.name: minced pork or mixed pork and beef

steps: Cook the buckwheat in twice its volume of lightly salted water for about 15 minutes until the water is absorbed, then let it cool.
Fry the onion and carrot in a spoonful of oil until soft and let them cool.
Mix the buckwheat with the mince, fried vegetables, garlic, egg, salt and pepper until it holds together.
With wet hands shape into 12 to 14 small patties and dust them lightly with flour.
Fry the patties in the remaining oil for 3 to 4 minutes on each side until browned.
Stir the tomato paste into the water or stock, pour it over the patties, cover and simmer on low heat for 15 minutes.
Serve hot with the sauce, sour cream and a fresh salad.

title: Kutia (Ukrainian wheat berry, poppy seed and honey Christmas dish)

ingredients.name: hot water for the poppy seeds

steps: Soak the wheat berries in cold water overnight, then drain them.
Simmer the wheat in fresh water with the salt for 1 to 1.5 hours, until the grains are soft but still whole, then drain and cool.
Cover the poppy seeds with hot water and leave for 30 minutes, drain and grind them in a mortar or spice grinder until milky and sticky.
Soak the raisins in a little hot water for 10 minutes and drain.
Mix the poppy seeds, honey, walnuts and raisins into the cooled wheat.
Add a spoonful or two of warm water if too stiff, taste and add more honey as needed, and serve at room temperature.

title: Mandryky (Ukrainian sweet cheese pastries)

ingredients.name: farmer's cheese, quark or dry cottage cheese

steps: Mix the flour, 1 tablespoon sugar, baking soda and salt in a bowl.
Add the buttermilk and the whole egg and knead to a soft dough; cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Mash the cheese with the filling sugar, sour cream and vanilla until smooth and thick.
Roll out the dough to about 3 mm thick and cut into squares of about 10 cm.
Put a spoonful of filling in the middle of each square, fold the corners to the centre and pinch the seams shut.
Place on a lined tray seam side down, brush with the beaten yolk and bake at 190 C (375 F) for 20 to 25 minutes until golden.
Serve warm or cool, dusted with icing sugar if you like.

title: Medivnyk (Ukrainian honey cake from Lviv)
steps: Heat the honey, butter and sugar gently in a pan until melted and smooth, then cool for 10 minutes.
Beat the eggs into the cooled honey mixture one at a time.
Dissolve the baking soda in the warm milk and add it to the batter.
Stir in the flour with the cinnamon, ginger and cloves until you have a smooth thick batter, then fold in the walnuts.
Pour into a greased and lined loaf tin or 20 cm cake tin.
Bake at 170 C (340 F) for 40 to 50 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the tin, dust with icing sugar and, if possible, leave a day wrapped so the spices mellow before serving.

title: Palianytsia (Ukrainian hearth-baked wheat bread)

ingredients.name: strong white bread flour, plus extra for dusting

steps: Dissolve the yeast and sugar in the warm water and leave for 10 minutes until foamy.
Mix the flour and salt, add the yeast water and the oil and knead for about 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Cover and let the dough rise for 1 to 1.5 hours until doubled.
Shape it into a round loaf on a floured tray, cover and let it rise again for 30 to 40 minutes.
Heat the oven to 230 C (450 F) with a tray of hot water on the bottom shelf for steam.
Cut a half-moon across the top third of the loaf with a sharp knife and dust with flour.
Bake for 15 minutes, then lower the heat to 190 C (375 F) and bake for 25 to 30 minutes until the base sounds hollow when tapped.
Cool on a rack before slicing.

title: Pampushky (Ukrainian garlic bread rolls served with borscht)
steps: Whisk the yeast and sugar into the warm milk and leave for 10 minutes until foamy.
Mix the flour and salt, then add the yeast milk, egg and 2 tablespoons of the oil and knead for about 10 minutes into a soft dough.
Cover and let the dough rise for an hour in a warm place until doubled.
Divide the dough into 16 pieces, roll each into a ball and arrange them close together on a lined baking tray; cover and let them rise for 30 minutes.
Brush the tops with a little oil and bake at 190 C (375 F) for 18 to 20 minutes until golden.
While the buns bake, mix the crushed garlic with the water, the remaining oil and the dill.
Brush the hot buns generously with the garlic mixture and serve warm with borscht.

title: Paska (Ukrainian Easter bread)
steps: Stir the yeast and a spoonful of the sugar into the warm milk and rest for 10 minutes until foamy.
Beat the eggs with the remaining sugar, vanilla and melted butter, then stir in the yeast milk.
Add the flour, salt and lemon zest and knead into a soft, smooth dough; knead in the raisins at the end.
Cover and let it rise for 1.5 to 2 hours until doubled in size.
Grease a tall round tin or two smaller ones and press in the dough so it fills them about halfway; decorate the top with a cross or braid made of dough scraps.
Let the loaves rise again for 30 to 40 minutes until they reach the top of the tin.
Brush with the beaten yolk and bake at 180 C (350 F) for 35 to 45 minutes, covering with foil if the top darkens too fast.
Cool in the tin for 10 minutes and then on a rack.

title: Varenyky (Ukrainian filled dumplings with potato and onion)

ingredients.name: plain flour, plus extra for dusting
salt, plus more for the filling
sour cream and fried onions to serve

steps: Mix the flour and salt, add the egg and the warm water and knead into a smooth, elastic dough; cover and rest it for 30 minutes.
Boil the potatoes in salted water until soft, drain them and mash until no lumps remain.
Fry half of the chopped onions in the butter until golden and stir them into the mash with pepper and salt; let the filling cool.
Roll the dough out thinly on a floured board and cut out rounds about 7 cm wide with a glass.
Put a spoonful of filling in the middle of each round, fold into a half-moon and pinch the edges firmly closed so no filling can escape.
Cook the varenyky in batches in a large pan of salted simmering water; they are ready 2 to 3 minutes after they float.
Lift them out with a slotted spoon and fry the remaining onions in butter until deep golden.
Serve the varenyky hot topped with the fried onions and a spoonful of sour cream.
